name: abs-visitor-arrivals-direction

task.question: The OAD release for reference month M has just been published. For a country of residence, will short-term visitor arrivals to Australia in the first month not yet published (M+1) fall short of the same calendar month one year earlier?
task.prediction_time: The publication instant of the ABS Overseas Arrivals and Departures (OAD) release for reference month M, observed at a maximum of 43 days after month end (Aug 2026 released 2026-10-13, Jul 2026 released 2026-09-11, Apr 2026 released 2026-06-12; all 11:30am local). At that instant every month <= M is published and month M+1 - the target month - is the first unpublished month. Features are published series values for months <= M only; the target month's value and its year-earlier level never ship.

feature_documentation: every shipped level feature is an OBS_VALUE of the publisher's OAD_COUNTRY dataflow (SDMX 2.1, CSV column semantics documented in the ABS Data API user guide and the dataflow structure, fetched by this build): CAT_TRAVELLER=06 short-term visitors arriving, TSEST=10 Original, UNIT_MEASURE=NUM persons, TIME_PERIOD monthly. country_resid is a CL_OAD_ARRIVALS_COUNTRY codelist code (names recorded in summary.json and the release data dictionary). target_year/target_month_num are the target month's calendar. diff_* columns are differences of the shipped levels, documented in build.py's module docstring

measurements.frame: OBS_VALUE of the CAT_TRAVELLER=06 series at month M = target month T minus one, the last month published at the prediction instant; current vintage (ABS revises post-release, so this is stated as current-vintage with the cutoff a documented assumption)
OBS_VALUE at M-1 (two months before the target month)
OBS_VALUE at M-2 (three months before the target month)
OBS_VALUE at M-3 (four months before the target month)
OBS_VALUE at M-6 (seven months before the target month)
OBS_VALUE at M-12 (thirteen months before the target month); diff_yoy_m = val_m - val_m12 is the YoY difference observed at M, the persistence analogue - the sign the task must beat
val_m - val_m1, the month-over-month change at the prediction instant
val_m - val_m12, the year-on-year difference at the prediction instant
country (or area) of residence; 78 codes in the codelist, the in-panel visitor series carries 70; names recorded in summary.json

the target month T = M+1, the first month unpublished at the prediction instant; the time column and the conservative event key (positives cluster in calendar time through shared Australian conditions)
1 iff OBS_VALUE(T) < OBS_VALUE(T-12); exact ties are 0 and counted flat; both source values are excluded from the shipped columns

known_event.event: Australia's international border closure (March 2020) and reopening (from November 2021)
known_event.expected: 2020 target months overwhelmingly fall short (down share >= 0.75); 2022 target months overwhelmingly do not (up share >= 0.75)
known_event.source: ABS OAD panel; candidate record known_event_fixtures, measured in-panel at discovery 2026-10-22

border_closure_2020.source: ABS OAD; candidate record known_event_fixtures (border closed March 2020; measured both-category 2020 YoY down 1,492 / up 159 at discovery)

reopening_2022.source: ABS OAD; candidate record known_event_fixtures (reopening from November 2021; measured both-category 2022 YoY up 1,645 / down 9 at discovery)

prediction_instant.citation: ABS OAD release calendar, observed 2026-10-22: Aug 2026 released 2026-10-13 (43 days), Jul 2026 released 2026-09-11 (42 days), Apr 2026 released 2026-06-12 (43 days); next-release schedule Oct 2026 due 2026-12-15, Nov 2026 due 2027-01-19

row_selection.basis: rows are (country, target month M+1) pairs on the visitor series; eligibility needs the six feature months <= M and the label inputs (M+1, M-11) - a missing outcome is counted in unobserved_target, never a membership decision on future data; the latest period any feature reads is M

id_columns_note: row_id is country@target_month, unique by construction; no identifier repeats inside a split or spans two
positive_events_note: an event is one distinct target month carrying at least one positive: positives cluster in calendar time (shared Australian conditions move many countries together; the 2020 and 2022 fixtures are such months), so the month is the conservative cluster; per-country persistence is a second axis recorded as a property in the candidate record
